tldr: Nvidia released Flora, an open tool that labels robot videos. Nvidia says it costs 72 cents an hour of footage, against $88 with GPT-6 Astra. Nous Research added an official Meshy plugin, so Hermes can make 3D models from a description or a photo. Another Nous plugin gives Hermes its own desktop that a teammate can watch and take over. Anthropic is handing its Agent Skills format to an open, neutral group, so it is less tied to one company.

articles.title: Nvidia open-sources Flora to make robot video labeling 125x cheaper than GPT-6 Astra
articles.summary: Open data engine Flora labels an hour of robot video for 72 cents, vs $88 with GPT-6 Astra. Built on three fine-tuned Qwen3.5 models. Vendor figures.

articles.title: Hermes Agent gets an official Meshy 3D plugin
articles.summary: Ask Hermes for a low-poly model for Godot or a printable model from a photo. Meshy's API needs a paid plan; first month of Pro is $1.

articles.title: trycua Spaces plugin gives Hermes its own desktop that teammates can watch
articles.summary: Hermes gets a Linux, macOS or Windows space on your own hardware. Teammates can watch, step in and hand it back. Check isolation first.

articles.title: Nous opens Hermes Labs Plugins repo for community plugins
articles.summary: Experimental community plugins at github.com/nousresearch/hermes-labs-plugins. Some are unmaintained; forks are encouraged.

articles.title: Anthropic donates Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
articles.summary: Agent Skills began as a Claude Code experiment. It now sits beside MCP at the Agentic AI Foundation, so skill files are more likely to stay portable.

articles.title: Dario Amodei replies to a critique of Anthropic
articles.summary: Long reply to a critic. Says some criticized examples were mistakes, and defends the rest as part of Anthropic's long-held strategy.
